jobs.title: Principal Development Management Officer
jobs.description:
Our benefits

Here at North Northamptonshire Council, we’re transforming for the better, using all our creativity and imagination to create the best life for our local people.

You’ll find that we have a wide range of careers that may be more surprising than you think!

Why choose us?

We offer a vibrant working environment with:

* a competitive salary
* a pension scheme, where we pay a significant contribution on top of your contribution. It provides life cover and ill-health protection.
* lots of opportunities to develop your skills, knowledge and potential in a large unitary council
* generous leave entitlement (28 days, rising to 33 days) and bank holidays, plus the option to buy up to an extra 10 days
* hybrid and flexible working arrangements, where practicable for service needs to help you with a healthy work-life balance.

We provide a range of great benefits such as an Employee Assistance Programme, an Employee Benefits Scheme, wellbeing support, travel rates at HMRC rates, as well as supporting a range of active Employee Network Groups.

About the role

North Northamptonshire Council is a product of local government reorganisation which took place across Northamptonshire in 2021. We have brought together the four former district and borough and county Local Planning Authority planning functions and working through a transformation programme to create a single high-performing planning service for North Northamptonshire.

North Northamptonshire is a high-growth area offering an exciting opportunity for professional development. We are working on preparing a new Local Plan to provide a spatial vision for the whole area. We are delivering sustainable urban extensions in differing phases of development, a wealth of large commercial and industrial development proposals and everything in between. This is a role that can offer a breadth of opportunities to utilise your knowledge and experience, and develop your career, in a job that is both challenging and rewardi

What will you be doing?

In this dynamic role you will play a vital part in supporting the effective delivery of North Northamptonshire’s planning functions. You will be at the forefront of providing customer service, engaging with a range of internal and external stakeholders, including members of the public, applicants and councillors, ensuring every interaction reflects our commitment to the future of our area.

You will be joining us at an exciting time as we implement our new team structure, come together in new headquarter offices, and roll-out new planning software and ways of working. Working as a Principal Development Management Officer you will be at the at the forefront of supporting initiatives be part of our continuing transformation and improvement journey, influencing the evolution of our service.

You will be responsible for a case load of some of the more significant planning applications, including the carrying out of site inspections, research, consultations and assessment of the case. Making appropriate recommendations in accordance with the policies of the Council. As required, this will include the preparation of Committee reports on planning and other applications, and the presentation of these reports at the Planning Committee.

You will be part of a team structure that is designed to ensure that you can both benefit from the support and guidance of colleagues to help you achieve your potential, but also utilise your own knowledge to mentor junior colleagues. For example, through our ‘Development Team’ approach we will offer opportunities for all officers to be involved in bespoke project teams brought together to handle largescale and high-profile developments.

About you

You will hold a relevant degree and qualifications or have the appropriate experience that would allow you to be eligible for chartered membership of the Royal Town Planning Institute (or equivalent).

You will be able to demonstrate extended experience of being responsible for a full range of planning applications, including largescale/complex proposals.

Extensive knowledge of the English planning system, including legislation, the National Planning Policy Framework and best practice advice.

You are able to deliver excellent customer service under pressure.

About us

**Our Values and Behaviours**

Our values define who we are and how we operate, by forming the foundation for how we interact with our customers, colleagues and provide our services. They are also at the forefront of our decision making and delivery and are:

Customer-focused  
Respectful  
Efficient  
Supportive  
Trustworthy

Our key commitments help ensure that the priorities we make, now and in the future, maintain the necessary breadth of focus in those areas that we believe matter most.

**Disability Confident Employer**

We are proud to be a recognised Disability Confident Employer and is committed to providing an inclusive recruitment process and will offer an interview to disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for the role.

Our Employment and Disability Service provides bespoke support to individuals facing barriers to employment, helping them work towards their goals to start, stay and succeed in employment. For further information please click here The Employment and Disability Service (EADS) | North Northamptonshire Council

**Armed Forces Community**

The council obtained the Gold status award for the Defence Employer Recognition Scheme (ERS).

Further information can be found at Jobs and careers | North Northamptonshire Council (northnorthants.gov.uk)

About the role

### **Shape Places, Influence Communities, Deliver Positive Change**

Join a dynamic Planning Service where you'll play a key role in shaping the future of North Northamptonshire. Working across Planning Policy, Development Management and Enforcement, you will lead and support a range of planning projects, helping to develop planning policies, guidance and evidence that influence how the area grows and develops. Alongside this, you will manage planning applications and appeals, provide expert advice to customers and colleagues, and investigate breaches of planning control, taking appropriate enforcement action where required. This varied role offers the opportunity to make a tangible impact on local communities by supporting sustainable development, protecting environmental quality and ensuring a fair, effective and trusted planning system.

What will you be doing?

* Support senior planning officers and managers in delivering Planning Service objectives.
* Provide excellent customer service and respond to planning-related enquiries.
* Contribute to service improvements, process reviews and system enhancements.
* Maintain up-to-date knowledge of planning legislation, policies and best practice.
* Produce accurate, high-quality work within agreed timescales.
* Attend evening and weekend meetings, committees and public consultation events.
* Assist in developing planning policies, design guidance and Local Plan documents.
* Undertake research and gather evidence to support policy development and place-shaping initiatives.
* Engage with communities, stakeholders and partners through consultations and public events.
* Analyse planning data, monitor trends and maintain planning databases and monitoring systems.
* Provide planning policy advice on applications, corporate projects and infrastructure planning.
* Prepare reports, statements and evidence for planning appeals, examinations and legal proceedings.
* Support the procurement and management of specialist planning consultants.
* Help develop and utilise planning technology, including Geographic Information Systems (GIS).
* Validate planning applications and process planning submissions.
* Manage a caseload of planning applications and planning enforcement investigations.
* Conduct site visits, consultations and assessments, making recommendations in line with planning policy.
* Prepare and present reports for Planning Committee meetings.
* Negotiate improvements to development proposals.
* Advise applicants, developers, residents and stakeholders on planning matters.
* Work collaboratively with internal departments and external organisations to achieve positive planning outcomes.
* Represent the Council at hearings, inquiries and court proceedings where required.
* Assist with complaints handling and support investigations undertaken by the Local Government Ombudsman.

About you

* A relevant degree or equivalent qualification to allow future access to Chartered membership of the Royal Town Planning Institute (or equivalent).
* Demonstration of a Personal Development Plan that explains a commitment via Licentiate, Associate or the Experienced Practitioner route, to achieving Chartered Membership of the Royal Town Planning Institute (or equivalent).
* Conversant with policy documents, plans, maps and architectural drawings.
* Understanding of the English Planning System.
* Experience of using computer databases, and Microsoft packages such as PowerPoint, Excel, Word and Outlook
* Good communication skills
* Report writing skills
* Able to deliver excellent customer service under pressure
* Good organisational skills
* Able to travel independently to multiple sites across the Council’s administrative area to undertake site visits on a frequent basis (3-5 times a week), or further away to attend meetings and events on behalf of the Council. For example, the ability to drive with access to own transport.
* Good time management skills
* The ability to carry out site visits or investigations on a variety of outdoor door locations including domestic properties, overgrown site with uneven ground conditions, and building sites

The post directly supports the delivery of major place‑based programmes in Barrow, including Brilliant Barrow and Barrow Rising, contributing to long‑term regeneration, resilience, and infrastructure improvement across the area.

This role supports the Council’s range of highway development management functions, including:

* Assessing planning applications and enquiries that affect highways, providing formal Local Highway Authority responses.
* Reviewing Transport Statements, Transport Assessments and Travel Plans and monitoring implementation on development sites.
* Negotiate mitigation measures, financial contributions and infrastructure improvements, including supporting Section 106 and Section 278 drafting and management.

* Engage with communities, partners, technical groups and elected members to promote collaborative working.

You will lead on specialist areas depending on experience—such as highways in new developments, or stakeholder engagement. jobs.title: Assistant Town Planner
jobs.description:
Union: HEA

Position: Assistant Town Planner

Pay Grade: 9

Pay Range: $33.71-$41.65 per hour (35 hours per week)

**Position Title:** Assistant Planner

**Department:** Planning

**Statement of Duties**

Under the general direction of the Town Planner, responsible for pro­viding technical assistance to the Planning Board concerning applica­tions for development, and assisting the Planner in carrying out the functions of the department.

**Essential Functions**

*The essential functions or duties listed below are intended only as illustration of the various types of work that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position.*

* Meeting with developers, attorneys, engineers, architacts, sur­veyors, contractors and members of the general public regarding Harwich regulations, procedures and application requirements.
* Reviewing applications for site plans, subdivisions, approval ­not-required plans and special permits as well as Zoning Board of Appeals referrals to determine application completeness, zon­ing compliance and adherence to Planning Board Rules and Regula­tions.
* Performing site inspections of properties which are the subject of development applications, accurately assessing existing conditions and applying information gathered to overall analysis of develop­ment proposals.
* Communicating with applicants and/or their agents to verify informa­tion or obtain additional data or plan revisions.
* Preparing memoranda on the findings and recommendations resulting from the development review process and delivering said memoranda and copies of plans to Board members prior to the meeting at which they will be discussed.
* Scheduling applications for review by the Planning Board and pre­paring agendas for the Board's meetings and attending said meet­ings; may also include taking minutes of meetings in the absence of a recording clerk and making presentations as needed.
* Following-up in unresolved Planning Board business at the request of the Board, including drafting of letters, writing formal deci­sions of the Board for filing with the Town Clerk, communicating information between the Board and Town officials, and gathering of pertinent information.
* Responsible for performing background research of grant needs and oppor­tunities which shall include regular communication with key people in each of the functional areas of Town government and continued review of grant opportunities from various sources; may also prepare grant propo­sals and aid the implementation of grants.
* When authorized, may serve to represent the Planning Board, Town or Town Planner/Grant writer in conferring with Town, regional, state and federal officials or with other public and private organizations on matters con­cerning planning, community development or grants.

**Supervision**

Incumbent works under the general direction of the Planner, but is expected to exercise prudent independent decisions and judgment. Does not supervise others, but may occasionally provide work direction to a clerical employee to ensure correctness of format and planning terminology and phraseology.

**Recommended Minimum Qualifications**

**Education and Experience**

Should possess a bachelor's degree (masters degree preferred) in urban planning or related field, such as: geography, engineer­ing or other field plus at least two years experience in the planning field during which time candidate should have had work experience in planning research and in working with state/local laws dealing with planning matters. Candidate must be able to demon­strate possession of the required knowledge, skills and abilities to perform the work of the position.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

A candidate for this position should have:

* Considerable knowledge of the principles and practices of town planning;
* Considerable knowledge of state and local laws relating to planning, zoning and related matters;
* Working knowledge of the economic, sociological and environ aspects of planning;
* Working knowledge of federal and state grant programs relating to local government;
* Working knowledge of personnel computer functions and operations;
* Ability to carry out planning and grant research, and
* Strong written, oral and graphic communication skills.

**Licensing and Certifications**

Must possess or be able to obtain a valid Massachusetts motor vehicle operator's license

**Tools and Equipment Used**

Equipment operated includes: Computers, software, related peripherals and general office equipment.

**Physical Demands**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl; talk, see or hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.

**Work Environment**

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Work is performed in an office setting and outdoors conducting site inspections. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is exposed to construction sites and equipment; loud noises and vibrations; fumes, gases and air borne particles; dilapidated structures and buildings and outside weather conditions. Frequent driving to various sites is required.

jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
Headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama, Moultrie (www.moultrie.com) is the leader in game feeders and cellular camera innovation, building products used by hunters, property owners, and others for real-time remote monitoring.

  

We take pride in developing deep user understanding, obsessing about the details, and going the extra mile to show our users we love them. Moultrie is customer-driven – hardware, software, marketing, and customer success teams collaborate to deliver a quality user experience.

  

**We are guided by the following principles:** Customer Obsession.; Excellence is the Standard.; Bias for Action.; Act Boldly.; Deliver Results.; Hire and Develop the Best.; Be Curious and Learn.; Win as a Team

  

**Job Summary**
---------------

Moultrie is seeking to hire a GIS Analyst to expand geospatial support across engineering, product, and data-focused teams. This is a full-time, exempt role reporting to the Senior GIS Developer. This individual contributor role will research and document key geospatial data sources that will power map products, spatial analytics, and inform business decisions. The analyst will support and execute against established priorities while helping refine processes as GIS capabilities grow across the organization.

  

Moultrie is actively growing its geospatial capabilities across existing map-based mobile and web applications, and support for machine learning and data science workflows. This role helps ensure geospatial data is identified, acquired, transformed, documented, and delivered with quality and reliability.

**Job Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Support the GIS team by researching commercial and open geospatial data.
* Acquire, clean, transform, and document geospatial datasets to support product, engineering, and analytics use cases.
* Conduct spatial analysis to quantify customer activity, feature utilization, and geographic engagement patterns.
* Execute against defined priorities and deadlines while raising risks early and communicating status clearly.
* Perform quality assurance checks to improve data completeness, consistency, and usability.
* Document data lineage, transformation methods, assumptions, and known gaps (for example, counties/states with missing data).
* Contribute to repeatable geospatial processes and help improve internal GIS standards over time.
* Support occasional off-hours on-call needs for geospatial operations.
* Participate in interviews and provide hiring feedback when requested.
  

**What Success Looks Like**

* Priority geospatial data sources are identified and delivered by agreed deadlines with clear documentation.
* Data products are complete where possible, with clear documentation of missing or unavailable data.
* GIS data research acquisition workflows are repeatable, documented, and trusted by partner teams.
* Cross-functional teams can reliably use geospatial analysis for planning.

**Job Requirements**
--------------------

* 3+ years of professional GIS experience.
* Hands-on experience with QGIS, PostGIS, GDAL, Mapbox, Python, and SQL.
* Strong understanding of foundational Geospatial concepts
* Experience collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders and communicating technical details clearly.
* Strong attention to detail, time management, curiosity, and ownership mindset.
  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 5+ years of GIS experience.
* Experience supporting geospatial needs for product teams.
* Familiarity with cloud computing in Microsoft Azure.
* Experience with Spatiotemporal Asset Catalogs (STAC) and cloud native geospatial formats.

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* The funding and long-term focus of a privately-held company, combined with the energy of a startup.
* The opportunity to work with cutting edge geospatial tools in an emerging GIS team.
* Remote-friendly culture with an optional annual hunting trip.

We are an equal opportunity employer and comply with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. We strictly prohibit and do not tolerate discrimination against employees, applicants, or any other covered persons because of race, color, sex, pregnancy status, age, national origin or ancestry, ethnicity, religion, creed, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including, but not limited to, hiring, training, promotion, discipline, compensation, benefits, and termination of employment.

  

We comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), as amended by the ADA Amendments Act, and all applicable state or local law.

At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we challenge what is currently accepted so we can deliver innovative and lasting solutions for our clients and communities. As an **Urban Planner**, you’ll help shape the future of complex development and infrastructure projects by supporting planning, due diligence, and site development efforts across a variety of markets, including data centers, advanced manufacturing, commercial, and industrial developments.

  
  

You’ll work closely with multidisciplinary teams to evaluate development opportunities, navigate regulatory requirements, and develop strategic planning solutions that support client objectives. Your contributions will help inform site selection decisions, advance permitting and entitlement strategies, and deliver master plans that enable successful project execution.

  
  

**What you'll do**

* Lead due diligence, entitlement, and site evaluation activities for development and infrastructure projects
* Research and interpret zoning ordinances, land use regulations, permitting requirements, and development codes
* Prepare and coordinate site master plans and conceptual land use plans
* Collaborate with engineering and technical teams to assess project requirements and development constraints
* Evaluate site opportunities and risks related to access, utilities, environmental considerations, grading, stormwater management, and infrastructure
* Coordinate planning activities across multidisciplinary teams and facilitate discussions to help resolve project challenges
* Prepare planning reports, site analyses, and client-facing deliverables
* Support projects from due diligence and master planning through transition to detailed design
* Deliver high-quality planning solutions that align with client goals and regulatory requirements

Here's what you'll need

* Bachelor’s degree in Planning, Geography, Environmental Studies, Engineering, or a related field
* 4+ years of professional planning experience
* Experience researching and interpreting planning policy, zoning regulations, permitting requirements, and development approvals
* Experience supporting site assessments, development feasibility studies, due diligence efforts, and infrastructure planning projects
* Strong stakeholder engagement and coordination skills
* Experience leading or supporting multidisciplinary project teams
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and planning-related software tools
* Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to effectively engage clients, agencies, and project teams
* Ability to travel to project sites as needed
  

**Ideally, you'll also have**

* Master’s degree in Planning, City and Regional Planning, Urban Planning, or a related discipline
* Experience supporting large-scale infrastructure, transportation, utility, commercial, industrial, or land development projects
* Experience preparing site master plans, land use studies, or development feasibility assessments
* Experience supporting permitting, entitlement, or regulatory approval processes
* Familiarity with GIS, AutoCAD, Adobe Creative Suite, or similar planning and mapping tools
* Experience working in a multidisciplinary consulting environment
* Participation in professional planning organizations

jobs.title: Senior Urban Planning Project Manager
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

**Work with Us. Change the World.**

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

AECOM’s Urbanism + Planning practice is a continuum of design vision and strategic advisory that transforms communities. We lead through integration, shaping the social infrastructure that connects us all. U+P’s primary focus includes urban planning, urban design, landscape architecture, workplace strategy, business transformation, asset advisory, economics, and environmental planning.

With a range of expertise from strategy and design through project realization, we create better outcomes to grow economies, protect natural systems, conserve natural resources, make societies more equitable, and connect and engage people through innovative, sustainable design solutions.

 **Job Description**

**AECOM** is seeking a Senior Urban Planning Project Managerto support our growing Buildings & Places Business Line. At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. AECOM’s Urbanism + Planning team is seeking a creative and experienced urban planner or urban designer to join its practice to manage and contribute to complex projects.

The role will lead transformative, large-scale urban design and master planning projects across the East Coast, with a focus on TOD, mixed-use development, placemaking, downtown revitalization, and public realm design in the Washington, DC region. Working collaboratively with urban designers, planners, landscape architects, engineers, and economists, the urban planner or urban designer will provide planning and urban design leadership, project management, client engagement, and business development for municipal, state, and private-sector clients.

Our teams have worked on transformative planning and urban design projects for high profile clients through the United States, including for major transit, transportation, economic development, and planning agencies.

The job responsibilities for the position will include but are not limited to:

Project Management & Leadership:

* In partnership with various Urbanism + Planning studios, lead complex, multidisciplinary projects from concept through implementation, including master plans, economic development strategies, land use and built form studies, public realm strategies, placemaking initiatives, and urban design guidelines.
* Manage project scope, schedule, budget, work plans, and deliverables across multiple concurrent projects, project phases, and multidisciplinary teams.
* Establish and maintain planning and urban design direction, quality, and consistency throughout project delivery while balancing innovation, feasibility, budget, and schedule.

Technical Support & Plan Production:

* Prepare conditions assessments, land use and real estate analysis, diagrams and renderings, and high-quality presentations and reports that effectively communicate planning concepts, economic development considerations, and urban design vision for complex projects.
* Lead and coordinate interdisciplinary teams, integrating civil, structural, transportation, environmental, landscape, and other technical disciplines into cohesive and viable planning and urban design solutions.
* Translate complex planning and urban design concepts into clear, compelling diagrams, visualizations, reports, and presentations for a range of audiences.
* Lead stakeholder engagement strategies and creative outreach efforts, including brand development, professional templates and style guides, event planning, meeting facilitation, online forums, and digital tools.

Client Relationships & Business Development:

* Lead and support client presentations, workshops, stakeholder meetings, and public engagement sessions with confidence, enthusiasm, and clarity.
* Lead and support proposal development, scopes of work, fee and budget development, work plans, and project interviews.
* Support client relationship-building efforts, identifying opportunities to expand existing relationships and develop new business.
* Represent AECOM by presenting at industry conferences and through participation in organizations.

  
**Qualifications**

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

* BA/BS in Planning, Urban Design, Landscape Architecture or related field + 8 years of related experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
* Demonstrated project management experience on complex, multidisciplinary, large-scale planning, urban design, and economic development projects, especially in urban and mixed-use contexts

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

North Northamptonshire Council is a product of local government reorganisation which took place across Northamptonshire in 2021. We have brought together the four former district and borough and county Local Planning Authority planning functions and working through a transformation programme to create a single high-performing planning service for North Northamptonshire.

North Northamptonshire is a high-growth area offering an exciting opportunity for professional development. In this dynamic role you will play a vital part in supporting the effective delivery of North Northamptonshire’s planning functions. You will be at the forefront of providing customer service, engaging with a range of internal and external stakeholders, including members of the public, applicants and councillors, ensuring every interaction reflects our commitment to the future of our area.

You will be joining us at an exciting time as we implement our new team structure, come together in new headquarter offices, and roll-out new planning software and ways of working. Making appropriate recommendations in accordance with the policies of the Council. As required, this will include the preparation of Committee reports on planning and other applications, and the presentation of these reports at the Planning Committee.

You will be part of a team structure that is designed to ensure that you can both benefit from the support and guidance of colleagues to help you achieve your potential, but also utilise your own knowledge to mentor junior colleagues. For example, through our ‘Development Team’ approach we will offer opportunities for all officers to be involved in bespoke project teams brought together to handle largescale and high-profile developments.

About you

Extensive knowledge of the English planning system, including legislation, the National Planning Policy Framework and best practice advice.

Under the general direction of the Town Planner, responsible for pro­viding technical assistance to the Planning Board concerning applica­tions for development, and assisting the Planner in carrying out the functions of the department.

*The essential functions or duties listed below are intended only as illustration of the various types of work that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position.*

* Meeting with developers, attorneys, engineers, architacts, sur­veyors, contractors and members of the general public regarding Harwich regulations, procedures and application requirements.
* Reviewing applications for site plans, subdivisions, approval ­not-required plans and special permits as well as Zoning Board of Appeals referrals to determine application completeness, zon­ing compliance and adherence to Planning Board Rules and Regula­tions.
* Performing site inspections of properties which are the subject of development applications, accurately assessing existing conditions and applying information gathered to overall analysis of develop­ment proposals.
* Communicating with applicants and/or their agents to verify informa­tion or obtain additional data or plan revisions.
* Preparing memoranda on the findings and recommendations resulting from the development review process and delivering said memoranda and copies of plans to Board members prior to the meeting at which they will be discussed.

Headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama, Moultrie (www.moultrie.com) is the leader in game feeders and cellular camera innovation, building products used by hunters, property owners, and others for real-time remote monitoring.

  

We take pride in developing deep user understanding, obsessing about the details, and going the extra mile to show our users we love them. Moultrie is customer-driven – hardware, software, marketing, and customer success teams collaborate to deliver a quality user experience.

  

**We are guided by the following principles:** Customer Obsession.; Excellence is the Standard.; Bias for Action.; Act Boldly.; Deliver Results.; Hire and Develop the Best.; Be Curious and Learn.; Win as a Team

  

**Job Summary**
---------------

Moultrie is seeking to hire a GIS Analyst to expand geospatial support across engineering, product, and data-focused teams. This is a full-time, exempt role reporting to the Senior GIS Developer. This individual contributor role will research and document key geospatial data sources that will power map products, spatial analytics, and inform business decisions. The analyst will support and execute against established priorities while helping refine processes as GIS capabilities grow across the organization.

  

Moultrie is actively growing its geospatial capabilities across existing map-based mobile and web applications, and support for machine learning and data science workflows. This role helps ensure geospatial data is identified, acquired, transformed, documented, and delivered with quality and reliability.

**Job Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Support the GIS team by researching commercial and open geospatial data.
* Acquire, clean, transform, and document geospatial datasets to support product, engineering, and analytics use cases.
* Conduct spatial analysis to quantify customer activity, feature utilization, and geographic engagement patterns.
* Execute against defined priorities and deadlines while raising risks early and communicating status clearly.
* Perform quality assurance checks to improve data completeness, consistency, and usability.
* Document data lineage, transformation methods, assumptions, and known gaps (for example, counties/states with missing data).
* Contribute to repeatable geospatial processes and help improve internal GIS standards over time.
* Support occasional off-hours on-call needs for geospatial operations.
* Participate in interviews and provide hiring feedback when requested.
  

**What Success Looks Like**

* Priority geospatial data sources are identified and delivered by agreed deadlines with clear documentation.
* Data products are complete where possible, with clear documentation of missing or unavailable data.
* GIS data research acquisition workflows are repeatable, documented, and trusted by partner teams.
* Cross-functional teams can reliably use geospatial analysis for planning.

**Job Requirements**
--------------------

* 3+ years of professional GIS experience.
* Hands-on experience with QGIS, PostGIS, GDAL, Mapbox, Python, and SQL.
* Strong understanding of foundational Geospatial concepts
* Experience collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders and communicating technical details clearly.
* Strong attention to detail, time management, curiosity, and ownership mindset.
  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 5+ years of GIS experience.
* Experience supporting geospatial needs for product teams.
* Familiarity with cloud computing in Microsoft Azure.
* Experience with Spatiotemporal Asset Catalogs (STAC) and cloud native geospatial formats.

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* The funding and long-term focus of a privately-held company, combined with the energy of a startup.
* The opportunity to work with cutting edge geospatial tools in an emerging GIS team.
* Remote-friendly culture with an optional annual hunting trip.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including, but not limited to, hiring, training, promotion, discipline, compensation, benefits, and termination of employment.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

AECOM’s Urbanism + Planning practice is a continuum of design vision and strategic advisory that transforms communities. U+P’s primary focus includes urban planning, urban design, landscape architecture, workplace strategy, business transformation, asset advisory, economics, and environmental planning.

With a range of expertise from strategy and design through project realization, we create better outcomes to grow economies, protect natural systems, conserve natural resources, make societies more equitable, and connect and engage people through innovative, sustainable design solutions.

 **Job Description**

**AECOM** is seeking a Senior Urban Planning Project Managerto support our growing Buildings & Places Business Line. At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. AECOM’s Urbanism + Planning team is seeking a creative and experienced urban planner or urban designer to join its practice to manage and contribute to complex projects.

The role will lead transformative, large-scale urban design and master planning projects across the East Coast, with a focus on TOD, mixed-use development, placemaking, downtown revitalization, and public realm design in the Washington, DC region. Working collaboratively with urban designers, planners, landscape architects, engineers, and economists, the urban planner or urban designer will provide planning and urban design leadership, project management, client engagement, and business development for municipal, state, and private-sector clients.

Our teams have worked on transformative planning and urban design projects for high profile clients through the United States, including for major transit, transportation, economic development, and planning agencies.

The job responsibilities for the position will include but are not limited to:

Project Management & Leadership:

* In partnership with various Urbanism + Planning studios, lead complex, multidisciplinary projects from concept through implementation, including master plans, economic development strategies, land use and built form studies, public realm strategies, placemaking initiatives, and urban design guidelines.
* Manage project scope, schedule, budget, work plans, and deliverables across multiple concurrent projects, project phases, and multidisciplinary teams.
* Establish and maintain planning and urban design direction, quality, and consistency throughout project delivery while balancing innovation, feasibility, budget, and schedule.

Technical Support & Plan Production:

* Prepare conditions assessments, land use and real estate analysis, diagrams and renderings, and high-quality presentations and reports that effectively communicate planning concepts, economic development considerations, and urban design vision for complex projects.
* Lead and coordinate interdisciplinary teams, integrating civil, structural, transportation, environmental, landscape, and other technical disciplines into cohesive and viable planning and urban design solutions.
* Translate complex planning and urban design concepts into clear, compelling diagrams, visualizations, reports, and presentations for a range of audiences.
* Lead stakeholder engagement strategies and creative outreach efforts, including brand development, professional templates and style guides, event planning, meeting facilitation, online forums, and digital tools.

Client Relationships & Business Development:

* Lead and support client presentations, workshops, stakeholder meetings, and public engagement sessions with confidence, enthusiasm, and clarity.
* Lead and support proposal development, scopes of work, fee and budget development, work plans, and project interviews.
* Support client relationship-building efforts, identifying opportunities to expand existing relationships and develop new business.
* Represent AECOM by presenting at industry conferences and through participation in organizations.
